title.en: Sound waves, their speed and the factors that change it

text.en: In a thunderstorm you see the flash first and hear the thunder a few seconds later. This is because light travels almost a million times faster than sound, and sound also needs a medium to travel.

Sound is produced by vibrating bodies and needs a material medium such as air, water or steel to travel; it cannot travel through a vacuum.
Sound waves are longitudinal: the particles of the medium vibrate along the direction of travel, forming compressions and rarefactions.
Waves below 20 Hz are infrasonic, those between 20 Hz and 20 kHz are audible, and those above 20 kHz are ultrasonic, which dogs, bats and dolphins can detect.
Light waves need no medium and are transverse, while sound waves need a medium and are longitudinal; sound in air travels at about 340 m/s but light at 3 times 10 to the power 8 m/s.
The wave velocity is the distance travelled per second; with wavelength lambda and frequency n it is v = n lambda.
Sound is fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases, v solid > v liquid > v gas, because solids are the most elastic.
For example sound travels at 5950 m/s in iron, 1493 m/s in water and 343 m/s in air at 20 degrees Celsius.
In a gas the speed is inversely proportional to the square root of the density, so a denser gas carries sound more slowly.
The speed increases with temperature, v = 331 + 0.61 T metre per second at T degrees Celsius, so it changes by 0.61 m/s for each degree.
Sound also travels faster in humid air, which is why we hear distant sounds clearly in the rainy season.

problem.en: A sound wave in air has a frequency of 500 Hz and a wavelength of 0.68 m. Find its speed. Find the speed of sound in air at 30 degrees Celsius.

why.en: Close to the speed in air.

text.en: v = 349.3 m/s, faster than at 0 degrees Celsius.

prompt.en: Explain why sound travels fastest in solids and why we hear far-off sounds better on a humid day.

requiredIdeas.en: Solids are more elastic than liquids and gases
Speed of sound increases with elasticity
Moist air allows sound to travel faster

commonMisconceptions.en: Sound travels faster in a vacuum

points.en: Sound is a longitudinal wave and needs a medium.
v = n lambda; infrasonic < 20 Hz, ultrasonic > 20 kHz.
v solid > v liquid > v gas.
v = 331 + 0.61 T; humidity raises the speed, density lowers it.
